yarn-troppo.meaning: All the science and safety points are kept, with colour that hangs off them ("Your spag bol won't glow in the dark.", "Conduction, the boffins call it."). Small additions stretch the facts: "with the boiling water exploding out of the cup and all over you", "so watch your fingers"; "in the past" is dropped from the FDA reports.
yarn-troppo.sense: Most terms fit ("tucker", "alfoil", "Bung something thick in there", "go easier on the power bill"), but "Fair dinkum, food done in a microwave oven may even hang onto more" uses "fair dinkum" for "In fact", a strain.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Largely natural ("like a littlie on red cordial", "Righto, containers."), with a couple of stock tags: "Fair dinkum", "Simple as that."
yarn-troppo.register: Heavier than level 3: a chatty yarn with an opening hook ("Ever wondered what's actually going on in that box on the kitchen bench?") and frequent asides. No swearing, fine at vulgarity 1.
yarn-troppo.tone: Informative and then serious where it matters ("This bit's serious, so listen up."), though the jokey asides lighten an official safety notice.
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads well aloud; the added "Sits there dead still, looking innocent." interrupts the explanation a little.
yarn-troppo.variety: Wide range: "tucker", "littlie on red cordial", "boffins", "Bung", "alfoil", "Righto", "listen up".
yarn-troppo.essence: Still the FDA explainer with its warning section, but retold as a kitchen chat.

dinkum-3.meaning: All points survive: the magnetron, reflection, water molecules, no inside-out cooking, energy efficiency, nutrients, containers, super-heated water and heating times ("Put the instant coffee or sugar in before you heat it and that cuts the risk right down.").
dinkum-3.sense: Terms fit: "till the tucker soaks them up", "alfoil", "knock the nutritional value out of your tucker", "the slightest bump or movement".
dinkum-3.authenticity: Natural, though "tucker" is leaned on and the opening "Now, the microwaves get made" starts mid-thought.
dinkum-3.register: A steady level 3: "stuff with heaps of water in it", "cos the food cooks faster", with the safety section kept plain. No swearing.
dinkum-3.tone: Informative and the warning stays serious: "can set off a violent eruption, with the boiling water exploding out of the cup".
dinkum-3.flow: Reads smoothly: "They bounce round the metal inside of the oven till the tucker soaks them up."
dinkum-3.variety: "tucker" appears three times ("the tucker soaks them up", "cooks your tucker", "out of your tucker") alongside a few other terms.

unharnessed.meaning: Every point kept, including the container tests ("They also cover how to test a container to see if it's right to go in the microwave or not.") and the warning about heating times.
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit: "Microwaves make the water molecules in your tucker jiggle about", "knock the goodness out of food", "you might wreck the oven".
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural on the whole; "Folks should stick closely to the precautions" uses US-sounding "Folks".
unharnessed.register: A little light for level 3; much is plain English ("Cooking in the microwave can use less energy than the regular way"). No swearing.
unharnessed.tone: Clear and informative, and the warning stays serious.
unharnessed.flow: Easy to read: "Even though the heat's made right there in the food, microwaves don't cook food from the".

yarn-dinkum.meaning: All points kept, from the magnetron to heating times ("make sure you don't go over the recommended heating times"); only "in the past" is dropped from the FDA reports, a trivial loss.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "the oven could cop some damage", "knock the goodness out of your tucker", "alfoil".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural ("the oven could cop some damage"), though "cooks quicker than other tucker" is a forced use of "tucker".
yarn-dinkum.register: Right at level 3, with plain technical content kept clear and a light Aussie overlay. No swearing.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Informative and the safety warning stays serious.
yarn-dinkum.flow: Smooth, with some repetition of "microwave oven" ("shouldn't go in a microwave oven at all", "shouldn't go in a microwave oven either").
yarn-dinkum.variety: "tucker" recurs ("the tucker soaks them up", "other tucker", "your tucker") and "cos" is frequent.

engine.meaning: The text is the original almost verbatim, so the facts survive, but the swaps garble a few lines: "When thick tucker are cooked", "tucker cooked in a microwave oven may keep more of their vitamins".
engine.sense: "tucker" is substituted for "food" even where it breaks the sense or grammar: "because tucker cook faster", "the heat of the tucker cooking inside".
engine.authenticity: Mechanical: "Microwaves cause water molecules in food to vibrate, producing heat that cooks the tucker." is US-official English with one word swapped.
engine.register: Essentially untranslated: "Users should closely follow the precautions and recommendations provided in the microwave oven instruction manuals". Only "tucker", "veggies" and "alfoil" mark it.
engine.tone: The official, cautionary tone is intact because the text is barely changed ("may result in a violent eruption with the boiling water exploding out of the cup").
engine.flow: The swaps break the grammar: "When thick tucker are cooked", "because tucker cook faster".
engine.variety: One word, "tucker", over and over ("absorbed by tucker", "cooks the tucker", "directly in the tucker", "cook tucker").
engine.essence: It is the original, so its content and shape are there, though unretold.

summaries.yarn-troppo: Lively and mostly natural, keeping the facts, but heavier and jokier than a level-3 brief for an FDA notice.
summaries.dinkum-3: Faithful and natural at the right weight; leans a little on "tucker".
